weather.tip: Clear and pleasant right now at 22.7°C, but a 93% chance of rain later today means showers are very likely — carry an umbrella and build in extra travel time, since Bengaluru traffic backs up fast once the rain starts.

around.headline: Bengaluru techie loses Rs 1.9 crore to fake trading platform pushed via Facebook ad
around.summary: A Bengaluru techie was duped out of Rs 1.9 crore after responding to a Facebook ad for a fake trading platform that showed inflated returns to keep him investing more, per The Times of India. Treat any investment ad promising guaranteed high returns as a red flag, and verify a platform's SEBI registration before putting in money.

around.headline: Bengaluru vegetable vendor duped of Rs 8 lakh in currency exchange fraud
around.summary: A vegetable vendor in Bengaluru was cheated out of Rs 8 lakh in a currency exchange fraud, per The Times of India. If anyone offers to exchange or convert cash for you, count and verify every note yourself and don't let them rush or distract you mid-transaction.

around.headline: BMTC staff go unpaid this month as free-ride Shakti scheme strains finances, says union
around.summary: BMTC has not paid salaries this month, with its employees' union blaming the financial strain of the free bus-ride Shakti scheme for women, per The New Indian Express. Regular commuters should watch for possible service disruptions if the pay dispute drags on.

around.headline: HD Kumaraswamy calls on residents to unite and protest over PRR-NICE link road
around.summary: Union minister HD Kumaraswamy has urged residents to unite and protest over the PRR-NICE link road project, per The Times of India. Those living along the corridor should expect continued disruption and possible demonstrations in the area.

around.headline: Karnataka flags hospital drug markups of up to 52.6 times the landing cost
around.summary: A Karnataka government review found some hospitals marking up drug prices as much as 52.6 times their landing cost, per The Times of India. Before buying medicines at a hospital pharmacy, ask if a cheaper generic or outside-pharmacy option is available — the price gap can be dramatic.

around.headline: Floods and landslides kill 56 in India, 14 in Nepal amid heavy monsoon rain
around.summary: Widespread floods and landslides have killed 56 people in India and 14 in Nepal as heavy monsoon rain continues, per Reuters. With Bengaluru itself forecast a 93% chance of rain today, it's worth postponing any weekend trip to hill routes like Coorg, Chikmagaluru or Wayanad until conditions ease.

events.note: Over 6,000 Bengalureans have united ahead of World Heart Day to support surgeries for 50 underprivileged children, per This Week India — a cause-based initiative running into tomorrow's observance.

events.when: Ahead of the Diwali travel season

street_smart.title: You're selling something quickly — a phone on OLX, a favour for a neighbour, closing out a shop counter. The buyer says 'Paid! Check your phone' and shows you a UPI screenshot with a green tick, a transaction ID and your name on it. Your own phone hasn't buzzed. They're already reaching for the item. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Evergreen topic — no single matching Bengaluru incident in today's feeds, but fake UPI payment screenshots are a persistent, recurring scam against shopkeepers and online sellers, and haven't come up in a Daily Pulse street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: The screenshot looks completely convincing — real bank logo, real-looking UTR number, even a timestamp from seconds ago. Free apps and simple photo editing can recreate this screen exactly, with no actual money moving. The buyer is polite but is already moving to pick up the item, treating the screenshot as settled proof.

choices.text: Accept the screenshot as proof and hand over the item right away — it looks official, and asking for more feels awkward.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. A payment screenshot is just an image — it isn't a bank record, and there are free apps built specifically to generate fake 'payment successful' screens with real-looking bank names, UTR numbers and timestamps. Once you've handed over goods or cash, that step is nearly impossible to reverse.

choices.text: Insist on waiting until you personally see the credit reflect in your own banking or UPI app (or get your bank's SMS/notification) before handing anything over — no exceptions for a screenshot.
choices.feedback: Correct. The only proof that can't be faked is the one that appears inside your own app or as an SMS from your own bank — never something shown to you on someone else's phone or forwarded as an image. Make this a habit for every UPI handover, however small or rushed the transaction feels.

choices.text: Tell the buyer UPI seems risky and ask them to pay cash instead.
choices.feedback: Risky. Switching to cash sidesteps this particular trick but doesn't actually teach you how to safely accept UPI, which you'll keep using constantly — and cash has its own well-known trap in fake or counterfeit notes, especially in a rushed handover.

choices.text: Call your bank's customer care to confirm the payment before handing over the item.
choices.feedback: Risky. Customer care can't instantly confirm one specific incoming UPI credit over a phone call, and the wait is unnecessary — your own app or SMS alert already gives you that confirmation faster and more reliably.

takeaways: A 'payment successful' screenshot proves nothing on its own — it's just an image, and free tools exist purely to generate fake ones with a real-looking bank name, UTR number and timestamp.
Only trust the credit notification that arrives inside your own banking or UPI app, or as an SMS from your own bank — never one shown or forwarded to you by the person paying.

For UPI, generate the request yourself (your own QR code or a Collect Request) rather than accepting someone else's screenshot as proof, and glance at your own notification bar before handing over goods or unlocking a service.

quiz.question: How much did a Bengaluru techie lose to a fake trading platform advertised on Facebook, per today's report?
quiz.why: The scam kept showing inflated returns on a fake dashboard to convince the victim to keep investing more — a common tactic in fake trading-app fraud, which is why verifying a platform's SEBI registration before investing matters.

quiz.question: According to a Karnataka government review reported today, hospital drug markups can run up to how many times the landing cost?
quiz.why: Such wide gaps happen because many drugs aren't under direct price control — asking for a generic alternative or comparing an outside pharmacy's price can save a lot.

quiz.question: How many people were killed by floods and landslides in India, per today's Reuters report?
quiz.why: Nepal separately reported 14 deaths in the same spell of heavy monsoon rain — a reminder that hill routes popular with Bengaluru travellers can turn risky during active monsoon weather.

quiz.question: Bengaluru's primary drinking water supply is pumped from which river, roughly 100 km away — one of the highest lifts of its kind in the world?
quiz.why: Water is lifted from the Cauvery at T.K. Halli and pumped uphill to the city, which is why supply is especially vulnerable to power outages and drought years upstream.

quiz.question: In economics, what does 'inflation' primarily measure?
options: The rate at which the general price level of goods and services rises over time
The total value of a country's exports
The unemployment rate in an economy
quiz.why: India's central bank, the RBI, targets retail (CPI) inflation of 4%, with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2 percentage points.
